intent: I live in Queen's Harbour Yacht & Country Club (a gated community in the City of Jacksonville). Does the association let me put artificial turf in my yard, where on the lot, what limits apply to a lagoon, pond, marsh or golf-course lot, and what exactly do I submit to the ARB and when?
distinctValue: Queen's Harbour publishes a dated turf rule of its own. QHRRP 5000-375 (SOD), revised 14 Oct 2024, recommends St. Augustine sod but permits artificial turf in the rear of the property per Fla. Stat. 720.3045, and then sets lot-type limits the Jacksonville page cannot hold: lagoon and retention-pond lots sodded or planted with approved Florida-Friendly ground cover to the water's edge; conservation-easement lots may not sod past the jurisdictional wetland line on the site survey; golf-course lots sodded to the cart path or sidewalk edge; every right-of-way sodded to the back of curb. The policy's own note paraphrases 720.3045 as covering items not visible from the frontage or an adjacent parcel, while the statute text (checked 2026-09-12) also names an adjacent common area and a community golf course, so a golf-facing rear yard is relying on the association's policy rather than the statute. Other checked local rules on the page: QHRRP 5000-131 (rev. 18 Mar 2026) requires a permanent swale on the rear of all lots adjacent to the lagoon or retention ponds, and Rule 62-308.100(5)(b) bars synthetic turf within a swale; 5000-305 bars filling, excavating or removing surface material in conservation easements; 5000-355 bars added soil or fill in natural areas and requires a 5-foot mulched edge; 5000-310 requires 100 percent automatic irrigation coverage of planted areas while Rule 62-308.100(6)(a) bars in-ground irrigation of synthetic turf; the ARB process in 5000-001 (rev. 09 Feb 2026), 5000-400, 5000-007 and 5000-009. UNSETTLED, put to the ARB Coordinator on the page: (1) whether a golf-course- or lagoon-facing back yard counts as 'rear of the property' for turf, given the sod-to-cart-path and sod-to-water's-edge requirements; (2) how far turf may run behind the house on a lagoon lot; (3) whether a back-lawn conversion is a minor (under 25 percent) or major (25 percent or more) landscape renovation; (4) how to show the irrigation zone under turf given 5000-310; (5) the ARB meeting time, which QHRRP 5000-001 gives as 4:00pm and the association's ARB web page as 3:30pm. CHECKED AND NOT USED: the 5000-020 fee schedule (no prices on the page); the legacy research's lot counts, listing prices, ZIP income and golf-course designer (demographics and unverified marketing figures); SJRWMD watering pages returned 403 on 2026-09-12, so watering days are left to the Jacksonville page; QHRRP 5000-500 dock and bulkhead approvals (not a turf rule); QHRRP 5000-005 definitions, which do not define 'rear'.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-375: SOD (Queen's Harbour Rules, Regulations & Policies), revision 14 Oct 2024
supports: Revision 14 Oct 2024
St. Augustine sod is recommended. However, artificial turf is permitted in the rear of the property per Florida Statute 720.3045 .
All waterfront lots abutting the lagoon, or a retention pond must be sodded or planted with an approved Florida Friendly Landscaping (FFL) ground cover to the water's edge.
Homes abutting conservation easements may not install sod beyond the jurisdictional wetland line which can be found on the property's site survey.

Sod must also be installed from the property line in the right-of-way to the back of the curb for a uniform aesthetic appearance throughout the community. Homes adjacent to the golf course must be sodded to the golf cart path or the sidewalk's edge.

Note: Per Florida Statute 720.3045 , owners and their tenants may install, display, or store any items on a parcel which are not visible from the parcel's frontage or an adjacent parcel, including, but not limited to, artificial turf, boats, flags, vegetable gardens, clotheslines, and recreational vehicles.
If you have any questions, please contact the ARB Coordinator at 904.221.8859 or email ARBcoord@qhycc.com .

sources.label: Fla. Stat. 720.3045: installation, display, and storage of items (2025 Florida Statutes)
supports: Regardless of any covenants, restrictions, bylaws, rules, or requirements of an association, and unless prohibited by general law or local ordinance, an association may not restrict parcel owners or their tenants from installing, displaying, or storing any items on a parcel which are not visible from the parcel's frontage or an adjacent parcel, an adjacent common area, or a community golf course, including, but not limited to, artificial turf, boats, flags, vegetable gardens, clotheslines, and recreational vehicles.

sources.label: Florida Administrative Code Rule 62-308.100, Synthetic Turf: adopted rule text (History–New 5-19-26)
supports: (1)(b) Pursuant to s. 125.572, F.S., this rule establishes minimum standards for the installation of synthetic turf on single-family residential properties of 1 acre or less in size.

(5)(b) Installation of synthetic turf must not alter the permitted stormwater management system as designed and shall not be installed within a swale, ditch, stormwater pond, or a stormwater pond's littoral zone.
(6)(a) In-ground irrigation systems cannot be used to irrigate synthetic turf areas.

(7)(b) Where no buffer zone has been established, synthetic turf shall be installed no closer than 10 feet from a natural or man-made waterbody as measured from the applicable ordinary or mean high water line except where there is a physical barrier between the synthetic turf and the waterbody (such as, but not limited to, a seawall or bulkhead).

(8)(b) Synthetic turf shall not be installed inside tree drip lines, whether on the property or adjacent properties, unless the tree is a noxious weed as defined by Chapter 581, F.S., or unless a certified arborist, using site specific information and best professional judgment, certifies that installation within that drip line would not be harmful to the tree.
Rulemaking Authority 125.572 FS. Law Implemented 125.572 FS. History–New 5-19-26.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-131: Drainage and Lot Grading, revision 18 Mar 2026 (CH1)
supports: Revision 18 Mar 2026 (CH1)

The owner and their contractor are responsible for establishing and maintaining positive drainage and following the approved drainage plan for Queen's Harbour (the plan is available at the POA Office).
No water drainage is to be diverted to adjoining lots.

A swale is a shallow channel with gently sloping sides usually to prevent drainage from going into the lagoon, street or adjacent property. A permanent swale is required in the front of lots on streets that do not have curbs and gutters and on the rear of all lots adjacent to the lagoon or retention ponds.

Prior to clearing and grading of any site in the Lagoon or adjacent to any water body, the contractor shall install silt screens/hay bales to minimize siltation/turbidity. These silt screens shall remain in place until all sodding/landscaping is complete.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-305: Conservation Easements, revision 14 Oct 2024
supports: All lots abutting conservation easements are subject to the restrictions set forth by the St. Johns River Water Management District (SJRWMD), the community's permits, and CCRE Article X, Section 10.6, as amended . All lots abutting the natural marsh areas are subject to these restrictions.

Vegetation within the conservation easement may not be removed or destroyed. This includes trees, shrubs or other vegetation. Easement land may not be filled with soil or any other material used as land fill. It may not be excavated or dredged and no surface material may be removed.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-355: Natural Areas, revision 14 Oct 2024
supports: Natural Areas are landward of the SJRWMD Jurisdictional Wetland Line and areas that remain in the same natural condition they were in prior to construction.
Additional soil or fill in these areas is not permitted.
Exposed edges adjacent to sodded areas, adjoining lots, etc., must be mulched to a minimum width of 5 feet with approved mulch types and maintained weed free.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-310: Irrigation, revision 14 Oct 2024
supports: All lots must be irrigated and shall adhere to the City of Jacksonville landscape and zoning code and current Comprehensive Plan requirements. The irrigation system must be designed to provide 100 percent (100%) coverage (except for the natural areas) for all planted areas, beds, etc., and must be fully automatic.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-300: Landscaping, New Construction and Major Renovation, revision 14 Oct 2024
supports: Major landscape renovation are changes affecting 25 percent or more of existing landscaping.
Every lot in Queen's Harbour is unique and each landscape design will be reviewed based on those unique characteristics.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-320: Landscape Drainage, revision 14 Oct 2024
supports: Plans must include the drainage pattern to be established on the lot for both new construction and major landscape renovations.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-007: ARB Application Determination & Appeal, revision 12 May 2025
supports: During the meeting projects will either Approved Tabled, or Denied
Note: A letter from the ARB will be issued to property owners with determination and any amplifying information.
This approval is contingent on the ARB Coordinator receiving the missing requirements within 14 days of the approval date.
The property owner has until the next scheduled ARB meeting to provide the requirements/document(s) outlined in the "Tabled" letter.
an application has been denied by the ARB: the property owner has the right to appeal the denial at the next regularly scheduled ARB meeting.
the ARB denies the appeal: the property owner has 30 days from the date of the ARB meeting that denied the application, to appeal to the Queen's Harbour Board of Directors.

sources.label: QHRRP 5000-009: Final Inspection Process, revision 12 May 2025
supports: Once the project is completed (on or before permit expiration date, including extensions) and ready for final inspection, the property owner must send to the ARB Coordinator via email… a photograph of the completed project.
The ARB will schedule the final inspection.

the property owner failed the final inspection: the property owner will have 30 days to bring the project into compliance and will be responsible for requesting, via email a reinspection from the ARB Coordinator.
